reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a high-return Ethereum bot, provides deployment instructions, and directs participants to fund the resulting contract with cryptocurrency. It presents reported returns of about 40 percent in a day and more than two Ether per week while describing a mechanism that profits by changing another trader's transaction price. Although the speaker acknowledges that profitability fluctuates, the video still includes a concrete funding requirement and unusually rapid return claims.

citations.quote: In this tutorial I'm going to explain an easy method to make passive income using decentralized exchanges like Uniswap.
STEP BY STEP INSTRUCTIONS:
Deposit funds (at least 0.1+ Ethereum to prevent negative slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
Click the deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain
the next step is to fund our contract with some Ethers to be able to snipe liquidity pools

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a guaranteed return. It expressly qualifies the outcome: profitability can vary, gas costs matter, and inadequate funding can cause losses from fees. That uncertainty is inconsistent with treating the earnings example as a certain result for every viewer. The description also explains a specific operational risk involving burn fees and recommends additional funding to cover it, which is a warning about conditions and costs rather than a concealment of them.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week-to-week
I've received messages from people who didn't fund the contract with enough Ethereum to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
The bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the headline and reported gains, but it omits the material qualification that profits fluctuate and that costs can consume funds. A claimed example of performance is not the same as a guarantee, especially where the speaker explicitly says the method is not always profitable. The funding language therefore does not by itself establish deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week-to-week
I've had some weeks where I've made 5-6 Ethers.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the overall message. The video still gives a concrete minimum deposit and then presents unusually rapid personal returns, including a gain of roughly 40 percent in a day. Saying results fluctuate acknowledges volatility, but it leaves the audience with an exceptionally attractive profit example while directing them toward a funded contract.

citations.quote: Deposit funds (at least 0.1+ Ethereum to prevent negative slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
something close to 40 percent, which isn t that bad
usually I make 2 plus Ethereum a week

opening.argument: The content is structured as an operational lesson about decentralized-exchange mechanics and smart-contract deployment. It explains what Remix does, identifies the Solidity version, walks through compilation and deployment, and describes the contract controls. That is consistent with a technology demonstration or tutorial, not necessarily a deceptive offer. The speaker says the method is easy to set up and provides procedural instruction, while the supplied material does not establish that viewers must pay the speaker or that the demonstration is a certification of guaranteed performance.

citations.quote: In this tutorial I'm going to explain an easy method to make passive income using decentralized exchanges like Uniswap.
Remix is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, deploy compile and launch smart contracts coded in the solidity language.
now click on compil3 bot.sole and wait for the bot to compile
the start button will start the bot sniffing the mempool

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not change what the tutorial instructs viewers to do. The steps include publishing the contract, funding it with Ether, and starting it to front-run transactions. The educational format is therefore being used to operationalize a profit-seeking scheme, not merely to explain blockchain concepts in the abstract.

citations.quote: Click the deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain
the next step is to fund our contract with some Ethers to be able to snipe liquidity pools
The last step is to click Start.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The prosecution's description of the steps shows practical instruction, but it does not prove that instruction is a scam. A working demonstration can include deployment, funding, and controls because those are the operations being taught. The supplied evidence also does not establish that the creator collects the funds or that the described example must be replicated successfully by viewers.

citations.quote: Remix is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, deploy compile and launch smart contracts coded in the solidity language.
Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week-to-week

opening.argument: This is presented as software and operational guidance for a blockchain trading tool, not as a request to transfer money to the speaker personally. The described workflow places funds in a contract, uses a start control, and provides a withdrawal function intended to return the initial Ether plus any profit. The materials also discuss gas and burn fees as possible costs. Those details describe a risky service-like tool and its operating conditions, but they do not establish a guaranteed-return deposit scheme, recruitment income, or a request for account credentials.

citations.quote: Withdrawal will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet.
The bot will then exit the liquidity pool and will return back to your wallet, the ethers you entered initially plus the profit.
the contract will waste a lot of gas fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The mechanism is not ordinary commerce merely because it has software controls. Viewers are told to send cryptocurrency to an exact contract address, activate it, and expect profits from another trader's slippage. The withdrawal button does not demonstrate that funds are recoverable or that the proposed mechanism works; it is simply part of the proposed transaction flow.

citations.quote: Deposit funds (at least 0.1+ Ethereum to prevent negative slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
Our bot will spot alice's transaction and buy unitoken at the price of $5.00, and increase the price so Alice will buy higher.
It will enable the bot to start sniffing the mempool to find different liquidity

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of recruitment or credential language is beside the point: the relevant concern is the combination of a funded contract and unusually fast returns. The withdrawal description is only the creator's account of what the button does; it does not independently verify that viewers receive their funds. The video also explicitly describes profiting by increasing another user's purchase price.
